text:
maria (Support): Acme reported spike in tail latency and wrong-region routing for a subset of requests. They say it started after a proxy update. They pasted example curl in thread, asked if router is ignoring client region header.

acme-app: Repro steps: curl to api.redwood.ai/v1/generate with header "x-client-region: ;eu" (note leading semicolon). We see responses from US edge, 200+ms extra RTT. We attached request_id 0a1b2c3d. No auth failures, just wrong edge.

maria (Support): Thanks. Can you paste the raw headers exactly as seen (including any cookie concat)? Also which SDK/proxy version?

acme-app: Raw header copied from their proxy: 
```
x-client-region: ;eu
x-other: value
cookie: session=abc; region=eu
```
Proxy version: acme-proxy v2.7.8. They suspect their proxy concatenates cookie region into header for legacy reasons.

maria (Support): Quick triage: router log for request_id 0a1b2c3d shows header value parsed as empty string. Router fell back to region default -> us-west edge. Log snippet: 
```
[router] req=0a1b2c3d x-client-region="" resolved_region=us-west fallback_reason=empty_header
```

tom (SRE): I pulled the raw TCP capture for that request. The header bytes are literally 0x3b followed by 'eu' (0x3b = ';'). I think our header normalizer treats leading non-token characters as missing value.

ingrid (Platform): That makes sense: our current header parsing trims whitespace but doesn't strip leading separators like `;` or `,`. Some proxies concatenate header fragments with `;` when merging cookie-like attributes.

ryan (eng-runtime): Quick patch idea: treat header value after trimming any leading `;` or `,` and whitespace as the intended token. Minimal change in router header canonicalization code. But want to be careful about accepting semicolon-delimited structured headers that are intentionally using params. Could we only normalize for `x-client-region` specifically?

maria (Support): Customer is fine with a targeted fix for `x-client-region`. They prefer not to change general parsing behavior right away. They also asked for a workaround they can deploy immediately.

tom (SRE): Workaround: ask their proxy to strip leading separators or set header explicitly. Example change in nginx lua: 
```
local h = ngx.req.get_headers()["x-client-region"] or ""
h = h:gsub("^[;,\\s]+", "")
gx.req.set_header("x-client-region", h)
```
If they can push that, immediate fix.

ryan (eng-runtime): I'll open a small PR to apply targeted normalization for `x-client-region` at the router entrypoint. Patch will: if header_name == "x-client-region" then header_value = header_value:gsub('^[;,\\s]+','') before validation. Adds unit + integration tests for leading semicolons/commas.

ingrid (Platform): Good. We'll canary that change in us-west first and watch for regressions. Any risk of changing semantics for customers who might intentionally include parameters?

ryan (eng-runtime): Low. This header is documented as a single token; params are not used. Tests will assert only token values allowed.

maria (Support): I told Acme the workaround and that we plan a targeted deploy. They applied nginx change and reported immediate improvement in their staging. Waiting on deploy to prod. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deploy started: router-canary v2026.03.17-1423 -> us-west (canary) by ingrid (Platform).

tom (SRE): Monitoring: no spike in errors, routing hit-rate for `x-client-region=eu` climbing in canary. Latency improved for Acme's test requests.

deploy-bot: deploy successful: router-canary v2026.03.17-1423 -> us-west (canary) completed.

maria (Support): Acme confirmed prod tests now route to EU edge and latency back to expected. They asked about any billing credit — we offered to review request invoice for the affected window.

ryan (eng-runtime): PR merged to main with targeted normalization + tests. I'll follow up with a changelog note.

maria (Support): Closing loop: customer satisfied, workaround provided, targeted parser fix deployed to canary then prod. Action items: (1) Ryan to push changelog + patch to stable; (2) Tom to check if other headers used for routing (x-customer-pref etc.) need similar handling; (3) Support to coordinate billing review with finance if customer requests credit.

acme-app: Thanks everyone, fixed on our side too after nginx tweak. Appreciate the fast turnaround.

maria (Support): Marking as resolved. Will file a short runbook note on this pattern (leading separator from proxies causes empty parsed header -> fallback).
